$comment: Every path this plugin delivers, and who owns it. Anything NOT listed here is the project's and is never touched. The update only ever touches a file the plugin actually changed between the installed and the target version.

classes.project: Created from a template once, then handed to the project. An update never rewrites it; when the upstream template changed, the update SUGGESTS how to fold that change in and lets the project decide. In practice these are rarely touched.
classes.plugin: Belongs to the plugin and is replaced on update. `project-specific: <id>` marker blocks inside such a file protect project content across the replacement.
classes.mixed: A plugin file where markers cannot work — the project's content and the plugin's are interleaved, or the format carries no comments. Claude merges these by hand, every time, always showing the diff.

REGENERATED, never copied. The plugin ships a row-less template; the project's copy is that header plus one row per installed guideline. Replacing it from source empties the table and every guideline silently stops being read. Rebuild the rows from `LIBRARY.md` for the files actually present in `.claude/guidelines/`.

rules: Before creating a new file, check whether the project already has one by that name; if so, resolve it explicitly instead of overwriting.
Only files whose plugin version actually changed between the installed and target release are touched at all.
Mirroring a plugin directory refreshes the listed files and deletes what a previous manifest listed and this one no longer does — anything else in that directory belongs to the project and stays.
Removing or moving a file: inspect what project content it holds first and resolve that case specifically. Never delete a path without accounting for the project's share of it.

A path in this manifest is the path IN A PROJECT. `source` is where it comes from in the plugin repo — always diff `git show v{current}:{source}` against the clone's `{source}`, never against the project path.
A `plugin`-class path the new manifest lists and the project does not have is INSTALLED, not skipped. 'Only changed files are touched' is about files that exist on both sides.

A `source` file ending in `.template` is delivered with that suffix stripped, unless the manifest `path` itself ends in `.template` (only `docs/specs/spec.md.template`, which the project keeps as a template). So `templates/guidelines/INDEX.md.template` lands as `.claude/guidelines/INDEX.md`.
The most specific path wins. `docs/specs/spec.md.template` is `plugin` even though `docs/specs/` is `project`; a directory entry never overrides a file entry inside it.
An entry with no `source` is project state the plugin does not author (`local-settings.md`, `context-*.md`, `docs/user/`, `LICENSE`, …). It is never diffed and never written by an update.

Where `source` is a directory but `path` is a single file, the plugin ships language/target variants and the project holds exactly one. Resolve the member from `variants` in `workflow-source.json`; if that is missing, detect it from the project's own file and record it. Never diff the whole directory.

`sourceBefore` records where an entry's source lived in earlier plugin versions. Use it when the installed version is STRICTLY BELOW the version it lists; at or above it the current `source` is correct. `git show v{current}:{source}` fails outright when the plugin renamed its own directory, and a failed OLD must never be read as 'new file, safe to overwrite'.
